canonical_data: store-backed conversation history and opt-in flow and agent-run checkpoints, by default as files under the home micro store directory
current_repo_note: A service framework that began in 2015 and gained agents later; the agent surface is the part reviewed here.
strengths: Existing service endpoints become agent tools through the registry, so an agent works with services a team already runs
Documented durability contract: flow steps checkpoint before and after each step, agent runs can opt in to checkpointing, and human-input pauses resume explicitly
The model layer covers several providers with retries and shared tool handling, on a codebase more than ten years old
weaknesses: The documentation says replaying an interrupted dispatch can create another agent invocation, and tool results are reused by name and input rather than call id
Recovery is explicit: persisting a checkpoint installs no background worker, and the default file store must survive the process
Go only; the agent features are newer than the service framework they sit on
why_it_matters: Shows the services-first route to agents: an established Go microservice framework whose registry becomes the agent tool catalogue.
